setup_cmd: D=~/fm-ex/ex-4-1-subagents; if [ -e "$D" ]; then echo "Already set up at $D. Run: cd $D (or delete it first to start over)."; else mkdir -p ~/fm-ex && cp -r exercises/ex-4-1-subagents/starter "$D" && cd "$D" && git init -b main && git add -A && git -c user.name=fm -c user.email=fm@example.com commit -qm starter; fi
title: Build a test-runner and a reviewer subagent, then fix a failing module
goal: Define two scoped subagents, a test-runner that reports only failures and a read-only reviewer, then use them to fix the bugs in src/cart.js. The tests must pass and neither subagent may have an Edit or Write tool (or, in Codex, a writable sandbox).

starter_prompts.claude: Create two project subagents in .claude/agents/: test-runner (tools: Bash, Read, Grep, Glob; runs `npm test` and reports only failing tests, never edits) and reviewer (read-only: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash; reviews `git diff` for bugs and missing edge cases). Then use the test-runner subagent to run the suite, fix src/cart.js yourself in the main session, and have the reviewer subagent review the diff before you finish. Do not edit anything under tests/.
starter_prompts.codex: Create two project custom agents as TOML files in .codex/agents/: test-runner (runs `npm test` and reports only failing tests, never edits files) and reviewer (sandbox_mode = "read-only"; reviews `git diff` for bugs and missing edge cases). Then spawn the test-runner agent to run the suite, fix src/cart.js yourself in the main thread, and spawn the reviewer agent to review the diff before you finish. Do not edit anything under tests/.

solution_notes: The subagents are narrow: the test-runner can run Bash but is told never to edit and to return a short PASS/FAIL summary, so verbose test output stays out of the main context.

The reviewer's read-only stance is enforced by configuration, not by asking nicely: no Edit or Write tool in Claude Code (it keeps Bash for git diff, so this guards against accidents rather than acting as a sandbox), and sandbox_mode = "read-only" in Codex, which the sandbox really enforces.
The fix stays in the main session. Subagents report, the main agent decides. Delegating the fix too would hide the diff from the conversation you are steering.

The four cart bugs are small (discount sign, free-shipping boundary, shipping decided on the discounted subtotal, thousands separators). The value of the exercise is the workflow, not the difficulty of the fix.
